title: Runtime <-> Simulator drift causing allowance calculation mismatch
creator: Ayesha Rao
description: Summary: We discovered a reproducible discrepancy between the decisions produced by the offline rate-policy simulator (used for QA and rollout validation) and the live runtime evaluator. The simulator reports identical traffic as ALLOW while the runtime occasionally DENYs the same request contexts under identical inputs. This causes confidence drift for policy rollouts and has caused two near-miss incidents where canary traffic was incorrectly classified as safe to increase capacity. Root cause appears to be a small normalization mismatch and different tie-breaking logic between the simulator's policy preprocessor and the runtime policy engine.
symptoms_and_observed_behavior:
- Simulator output: >95% ALLOW for test prompt set.
- Runtime output: ~3% DENY for same keys/routes when replayed through staging runner.
- Mismatch concentrated on multi-route policies that use weighted inheritance and per-org caps.
- Logs show divergent intermediate scores prior to final policy decision in runtime vs simulator.
reproduction_steps: 3) Load same traces into staging runtime replay harness: ./replay --target staging --traces traces.tar.gz
4) Compare decisions: jq -s 'map(.decision) | unique' sim-output.json runtime-output.json
5) Observe ~3% of entries where decisions differ (ALLOW vs DENY).
impact_analysis: Customer-visible impact is limited so far (no billing mismatch observed in production), but the mismatch undercuts our rollout safety checks: simulator may approve policy changes that runtime would reject, enabling unsafe canaries or incorrect autoscale decisions. Risk vector: high for enterprise customers using per-org caps and A/B model rollouts. Estimated RTO for critical regression if left unaddressed: 4 hours to mitigate via manual throttles.
initial_hypothesis: 1) Simulator preprocessor normalizes route aliases differently (order of map iteration changes a fallback weight). 2) Runtime uses floating-point scores with a different tie-breaker when multiple policies sum to the same allowance bucket. 3) Replay harness may omit a small metadata header used by runtime to compute org-level aggregated usage.
investigation_notes: - Confirmed that removing whitespace-normalization in simulator reduces mismatch but does not eliminate it.
- Added extra debug logging in runtime policy-eval: found that score aggregation applies rounding at different stage than simulator.
- Compared policy ASTs: simulator applies 'flatten-inheritance' pass in a different order than runtime compiler.
- Kernel of mismatch lies in two places: normalization (string->key) and numerical tie-breaking (score epsilon).
short_term_mitigation:
- Update simulator to import the runtime's normalization utility (PR: https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/14892) and re-run validations.
- Add an assertion in rollout pipeline to fail canary promotion if simulator/runtime disagreement > 0.1%.
- Instrument a metric 'policy_simulator_mismatch_rate' and alert at 0.05% to paging for oncall response.
proposed_long_term_fixes:
Option A (preferred): Standardize normalization and tie-breaking code by extracting common library used by both simulator and runtime evaluator. This avoids future drift but requires a small refactor of runtime to link the new shared library.
Option B: Make the simulator emulate the runtime behavior with a shim layer that mirrors floating point rounding and tie-breaking rules. Lower engineering risk but duplicates quirks.
Decision: pursue Option A to reduce technical debt. Will split into two PRs: shared-lib extraction + runtime refactor.
design_tradeoffs_and_constraints:
- Shared library improves correctness but touches hot path in runtime evaluator (must be optimized and thoroughly benchmarked).
- Backwards compatibility: must not change existing production behavior (we will gate runtime change behind feature flag 'policy-sharedlib').
- Testing surface: add cross-runner golden files and property-based tests to ensure deterministic evaluation across architectures (x86 vs arm64).
implementation_plan: 1) Extract normalization + tie-breaking logic to packages/policy-common (ENG-839777-A).
2) Update simulator to use policy-common and add integration test harness (ENG-839777-B).
3) Add feature-flagged runtime link to policy-common and run perf microbenchmarks (ENG-839777-C).
4) Canary rollout of feature-flag on staging orgs, monitor mismatch and latency (ENG-839777-D).
5) Flip feature flag for all regions after 48h verification and 0 mismatches observed for 24h (ENG-839777-E).
related_prs: https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/14910 -- add simulator <-> runtime golden test harness (draft)
tests_and_validation:
- Add end-to-end replay test that runs the same trace through simulator and runtime under the same linked policy-common.
- Add property tests that fuzz policy weights and verify invariant: decisions must be identical when inputs equal and environment flags equal.
- Add performance benchmark comparing runtime eval latency pre/post extraction (target <2% regression).
rollout_and_monitoring:
- Start with one staging region and two non-critical orgs. Monitor 'policy_simulator_mismatch_rate', 'policy_eval_p99_latency', and 'canary_denied_rate'.
- Create dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/billing/policy-safety?panelId=3
- If mismatch_rate rises above 0.02% or latency p99 regresses >5%, rollback feature flag.
timeline: Week 1: extract policy-common, update simulator. Week 2: instrument runtime, add tests and bench, run staging canary. Week 3: rollout to prod feature-flag for small orgs, monitor 48h, then ramp.
